Create a save point 1. **If you’re using Git** ```bash git add . git commit -m "Before safety checks – final launch prep" ``` 2. **If you don’t have Git** – zip the whole folder (except `node_modules`) and name it `lovable-launch-YYYYMMDD.zip`. > **Proof:** Commit shows a new “Ready for launch” tag or the zip exists. --- ### 2. Run the secret & usage checker 1. Open a terminal in your project folder. ```bash python3 /scripts/check_secrets.py . --report ship-check.txt ``` 2. Open `ship-check.txt`. * It should say **“No secret keys exposed in the public code.”** * It should list any paid services (Stripe) and suggest spending caps. > **If it reports a secret in the code** – copy that key out and create a corresponding entry in your environment file (`.env`). > For example: > ``` > STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_... > ``` > Then delete the hard‑coded key from any file and commit again. > **Proof:** The report ends with “All good – no secrets found in the repo.” --- ### 3. Verify Supabase RLS & policies 1. Open the Supabase dashboard → **Database → Policies**. 2. For every table (e.g., `posts`, `comments`, `users`) ensure: * **RLS is ON.** * There is a **policy** that allows `authenticated` to `select, insert, update, delete` on rows where `user_id = auth.uid()`. * Example policy text (copy‑paste if you click “Example”): ```sql CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can manage their rows" ON FOR ALL USING ("user_id" = auth.uid()) WITH CHECK ("user_id" = auth.uid()); ``` 3. Test locally or via the SQL editor: ```sql SELECT * FROM posts LIMIT 5; ``` – You should see only rows you own. > **Proof:** No policy error, only your rows returned. --- ### 4. Test the Stripe webhook locally 1. Install the Stripe CLI (if you haven’t): ```bash curl -L https://stripe.com/stripe-cli | bash ``` 2. Log in to Stripe: ```bash stripe login ``` 3. Forward the webhook to your local server: ```bash stripe listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/api/stripe/webhook ``` 4. Simulate a checkout session (on a test account) and watch the logs. * You should see a line like “Got event type invoice.payment_succeeded”. * No 500 errors. > **Proof:** The webhook receives events and your server logs a success message. --- ### 5. Run the “stranger” test 1. Open a new incognito window (no login). 2. Visit your app’s URL (e.g., `https://yourapp.lovable.io`). 3. Verify: * No private data visible. * No API keys in the page source (`sk_` or similar). * No “.env” or other config files accessible. * There is a “Login / Sign‑up” button. * No Stripe checkout form without signing in. > **Proof:** The page shows only public information and prompts for login. --- ### 6. Prepare the Product Hunt link 1. If you’re not already, set up a lightweight “Landing” page on your site that briefly explains the app and links to the sign‑up page. 2. Copy the URL of that “Landing” page (e.g., `https://yourapp.lovable.io/landing`). 3. On Product Hunt, paste that URL in the “App URL” field when you submit. > **Proof:** The launch post opens to your landing page. --- ### 7. (Optional) Add a privacy notice 1. Create a simple `privacy.md` in the root of your repo. 2.
